subject.name: Daniel Lurie
subject.dataPolicy: Uses balanced source collection plus public San Francisco datasets only. No approval ratings and no fabricated metric, status, or progress values.

workflow.name: Pull sources
workflow.description: Scheduled job gathers official mayoral releases, local reporting, broad web/news results, and public metric feeds.

workflow.name: AI extraction
workflow.description: Sources are summarized into announcements, promises, claims, topics, and evidence-backed next actions.

workflow.name: Human review
workflow.description: Low-confidence AI interpretations are flagged before they affect status labels or scorecards.

workflow.name: Visualize
workflow.description: Dashboard converts structured records into topic charts, progress bars, timeline items, and metric deltas.

sources.title: S.F. activists deliver 1,500 postcards to Mayor Lurie, asking him to stop budget cuts
sources.summary: The People’s Budget Coalition delivered over 1,500 postcards today to Mayor Daniel Lurie’s office today, demanding the mayor stop cutting funds to services.
sources.excerpt: Mission Local is growing Four new neighborhoods. Four dedicated reporters. Zero paywalls. Help us stay free for all of San Francisco. Donate today If you can’t get through to the mayor, try sending him a postcard. This was the strategy of the People’s Budget Coalition — made up of various nonprofits and other city-funded groups impacted by budget cuts — which delivered more than 1,500 postcards today to Mayor Daniel Lurie’s office. Each card was inscribed with an individual’s plea to keep the mayor’s budget cuts at bay. Those cuts have gutted many social programs, advocates say, including immigrant services and public-health initiatives . “People will die if these budget cuts move forward,” said Anya Worley-Ziegmann, coalition coordinator. The postcards were tied together with string, and activists lined up to deliver them to Lurie’s office. Representatives from different community groups — among them seniors and people with disabilities, neighborhood residents, and others from the HIV Advocacy Network — spoke to a representative from the mayor’s office, who stood outside, listened to each person, and took notes. Lurie’s office directed members of the press to the mayor’s remarks at a press conference earlier Tuesday morning. San Francisco is facing a $643 million deficit , and Lurie earlier this year instructed departments to cut programs, stop hiring, and review all contracts for potential savings. “We have to make painful decisions,” Lurie said during that Q&A. “I want to set our city up on firm financial footing, I want to think long term about the city.” Lurie has largely spared law enforcement from the cuts, however, and the city recently approved new police and firefighter contracts that would cost $100 million extra over two years. promises.text: Create an emergency shelter plan intended to end unsheltered homelessness in six months.

promises.text: Use emergency authority to accelerate city response to open-air drug markets and fentanyl-related street conditions.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting verified public safety, overdose-response, treatment-linkage, and budget/action evidence before assigning progress or delivery status.

promises.text: Keep Union Square activations running through summer 2027 to support downtown recovery.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting verified programming calendar, downtown foot-traffic, vacancy, sales-tax, and attendance data before assigning progress or delivery status.

promises.text: Publish and begin implementing an updated city Climate Action Plan.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting implementation metrics such as emissions inventory, building upgrades, energy-burden data, and funded actions before assigning progress or delivery status.

promises.text: Tackle fare evasion on public transit and make Muni more accountable.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting verified fare evasion data, enforcement metrics, and revenue impact before assigning progress or delivery status.

promises.text: Major expansion of free and low-cost childcare with hundreds of new spots for families with infants and toddlers.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting verified childcare capacity data, enrollment numbers, and program implementation timeline.

promises.text: Sign legislation to support San Francisco Police Officers and continue to drive down crime.
promises.statusNote: Awaiting verified crime statistics, officer retention data, and policy implementation evidence.

promises.text: Reach lowest level of unsheltered homelessness in 15 years.
promises.statusNote: Claim requires verification from official PIT count data and methodology review.

claims.claim: Downtown activations can support San Francisco's economic recovery by bringing more people to the core.
claims.evidencePlan: Compare Union Square foot traffic, hotel occupancy, retail vacancy, sales tax receipts, and event attendance before/after programming dates.

claims.claim: The updated Climate Action Plan can lower household costs while reducing emissions.
claims.evidencePlan: Track utility costs, retrofit adoption, emissions inventory, and household energy-burden datasets.

claims.claim: San Francisco has reached lowest level of unsheltered homelessness in 15 years.
claims.evidencePlan: Verify against official HUD Point-in-Time count data, methodology, and historical counts from 2011-2026.

claims.claim: New legislation will continue to drive down crime in San Francisco.
claims.evidencePlan: Track SFPD crime statistics by category, compare pre/post legislation rates, and verify causal relationship.

claims.claim: Major expansion will create hundreds of new childcare spots for infants and toddlers.
claims.evidencePlan: Obtain enrollment capacity data from city childcare providers, track new spots created, and verify income-eligibility criteria.

timeline.title: Daniel Lurie mayoral term begins
timeline.impact: Tracker baseline date for promises, announcements, public SF metrics, and review tasks.

timeline.title: Emergency authority for fentanyl response
timeline.impact: Moved public-safety response promise into implementation tracking.

timeline.title: Homelessness and behavioral health overhaul covered
timeline.impact: Created an early promise requiring shelter capacity, outreach placement, and encampment metric validation.

timeline.title: Union Square programming extended
timeline.impact: Added a measurable downtown recovery promise with foot-traffic and vacancy indicators.

timeline.title: Climate Action Plan update released
timeline.impact: Plan publication is observable; implementation still needs emissions and cost metrics.

timeline.title: First Executive Director of Arts and Culture appointed
timeline.impact: Matthew Goudeau appointed as city's first arts executive director, signaling arts infrastructure priority.

timeline.title: Steven Betz announced as new public safety chief
timeline.impact: New public safety leadership appointed to coordinate law enforcement and emergency response.

timeline.title: Major childcare expansion announced
timeline.impact: Hundreds of new free and low-cost childcare spots promised for families with infants and toddlers.

timeline.title: Plan to tackle Muni fare evasion announced
timeline.impact: New accountability measures for public transit fare enforcement and Muni performance.

timeline.title: Police support legislation signed
timeline.impact: Legislation to support SFPD officers and continue crime reduction efforts signed into law.

timeline.title: Unsheltered homelessness reaches 15-year low
timeline.impact: Major milestone claimed in homelessness reduction; requires PIT count verification.

timeline.title: Activists deliver 1,500 postcards opposing budget cuts
timeline.impact: People's Budget Coalition delivered postcards demanding mayor stop cutting funds to social services and immigrant programs.

reviewQueue.title: Budget cuts to social services

reviewQueue.title: Overdose 911 response trend analysis
reviewQueue.reason: Latest data shows 169 responses (March 2026) vs 30 baseline (Dec 2024); needs context on seasonal variation and fentanyl response effectiveness.

reviewQueue.title: Naloxone distribution decline
reviewQueue.reason: Distribution dropped from 55,904 (Dec 2024) to 41,664 (Sept 2025); needs explanation of decline during fentanyl crisis response.

reviewQueue.title: Housing permit issuance decline May 2026
reviewQueue.reason: Permits dropped to 674 in May 2026 from ~1,400 average; likely partial month data but needs verification.
